findings_qualitative.value: CO(3-2) is in clumpy filaments with no preferred orientation, many along dust lanes

evidence.quote: The CO(3-2) in He 2-10 is in clumps that form filamentary systems, and many of the filaments correlate with optical dust lanes.

findings_qualitative.value: No CO clump or unusual kinematics at the non-thermal radio source

evidence.quote: There is no CO(3–2) clump coincident with the non-thermal radio source that has been suggested to be an AGN, nor unusual kinematics.

claims.experiment: Channel maps and velocity field of the West filament
claims.result: Velocity gradient increasing toward western starburst
claims.finding: West filament is accelerating onto the embedded cluster

evidence.quote: The filament appears to be accelerating into the western starburst cloud

claims.hypothesis: Is the East filament a tidal tail?
claims.experiment: Moment 1 map along and across filament
claims.result: Shear of 20-40 km/s across width, no gradient along length
claims.finding: Tidal tail identification questioned; shear unexplained

evidence.quote: This calls into question Kobulnicky et al. (1995)’s original identification of this structure as a tidal tail.

claims.hypothesis: Is there a molecular outflow in the south?
claims.experiment: Velocity dispersion map and channel maps of the Bird
claims.result: σ up to 40 km/s, FWZI ~140 km/s
claims.finding: Molecular outflow with energy >=1e53 erg and no identified source

evidence.quote: The Bird appears to be a molecular outflow.

claims.hypothesis: Does the non-thermal source sit on a CO clump (AGN?)
claims.experiment: Compare CO map with VLA 3.6 cm
claims.result: Source lies on a molecular spur with quiescent kinematics
claims.finding: May argue for SNR rather than AGN

evidence.quote: The CO(3–2) kinematics there are quiescent, which may argue that it is an SNR rather than an AGN.
